SYSTEM ROLE

You are proposing auditable knowledge-component hypotheses for a controlled
English grammar-learning study. You are not being asked to discover human
cognitive truth. Return JSON only and conform exactly to the supplied schema.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY

You see a finite universe of canonical GrammarCells and their source-support
counts. You do not see the study's existing generator KCs, item bank, Q-matrix,
learner responses, simulator states, or downstream results. Do not infer that
the desired answer is one KC per feature value.

Propose between 12 and 24 reusable hypotheses. Each
hypothesis must have:

- a concise neutral name;
- a type: operation, construction_family, feature_value, interaction, or
  prerequisite_hypothesis;
- a pedagogical interpretation: what a learner might plausibly improve through
  practice;
- a parsimony/reuse rationale;
- an executable activation predicate using only the supplied grammar;
- a stated limitation or discriminating evidence that the GrammarCell schema
  cannot supply.

PREDICATE GRAMMAR

`activation.any_of` is a non-empty list of clauses. A clause is an `all_of`
object with exactly the six declared dimension keys. Each value is an array of
allowed values; an empty array means that dimension is unconstrained. At least
one dimension in every clause must have a non-empty array. A cell activates the
hypothesis iff at least one clause matches and every constrained dimension has
a value in its array. Enumerate values when you need a set such as all
modal-bearing cells. Do not use free-form code, regexes, negation operators,
item-format fields, lexical lemmas, or source IDs.

Prefer hypotheses that are linguistically coherent, reusable, independently
interpretable, measurable in more than one cell where the universe permits,
parsimonious, compositional, and pedagogically relevant. Do not add a column
merely to increase matrix rank. Do not treat response format as knowledge.
When the schema lacks distinctions needed for a good hypothesis (for example
modal function, lexical morphology, or person/number), say so rather than
fabricating them.

SYSTEM ROLE

You are proposing auditable knowledge-component hypotheses for a controlled
English grammar-learning study. You are not being asked to discover human
cognitive truth. Return JSON only and conform exactly to the supplied schema.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY

You see a finite universe of canonical GrammarCells and their source-support
counts. You do not see the study's existing generator KCs, item bank, Q-matrix,
learner responses, simulator states, or downstream results. Do not infer that
the desired answer is one KC per feature value.

Propose between 12 and 24 reusable hypotheses. Each
hypothesis must have:

- a concise neutral name;
- a type: operation, construction_family, feature_value, interaction, or
  prerequisite_hypothesis;
- a pedagogical interpretation: what a learner might plausibly improve through
  practice;
- a parsimony/reuse rationale;
- an executable activation predicate using only the supplied grammar;
- a stated limitation or discriminating evidence that the GrammarCell schema
  cannot supply.

PREDICATE GRAMMAR

`activation.any_of` is a non-empty list of clauses. A clause is an `all_of`
object with exactly the six declared dimension keys. Each value is an array of
allowed values; an empty array means that dimension is unconstrained. At least
one dimension in every clause must have a non-empty array. A cell activates the
hypothesis iff at least one clause matches and every constrained dimension has
a value in its array. Enumerate values when you need a set such as all
modal-bearing cells. Do not use free-form code, regexes, negation operators,
item-format fields, lexical lemmas, or source IDs.

Prefer hypotheses that are linguistically coherent, reusable, independently
interpretable, measurable in more than one cell where the universe permits,
parsimonious, compositional, and pedagogically relevant. Do not add a column
merely to increase matrix rank. Do not treat response format as knowledge.
When the schema lacks distinctions needed for a good hypothesis (for example
modal function, lexical morphology, or person/number), say so rather than
fabricating them.

SYSTEM ROLE

You are proposing auditable knowledge-component hypotheses for a controlled
English grammar-learning study. You are not being asked to discover human
cognitive truth. Return JSON only and conform exactly to the supplied schema.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY

You see a finite universe of canonical GrammarCells and their source-support
counts. You do not see the study's existing generator KCs, item bank, Q-matrix,
learner responses, simulator states, or downstream results. Do not infer that
the desired answer is one KC per feature value.

Propose between 12 and 24 reusable hypotheses. Each
hypothesis must have:

- a concise neutral name;
- a type: operation, construction_family, feature_value, interaction, or
  prerequisite_hypothesis;
- a pedagogical interpretation: what a learner might plausibly improve through
  practice;
- a parsimony/reuse rationale;
- an executable activation predicate using only the supplied grammar;
- a stated limitation or discriminating evidence that the GrammarCell schema
  cannot supply.

PREDICATE GRAMMAR

`activation.any_of` is a non-empty list of clauses. A clause is an `all_of`
object with exactly the six declared dimension keys. Each value is an array of
allowed values; an empty array means that dimension is unconstrained. At least
one dimension in every clause must have a non-empty array. A cell activates the
hypothesis iff at least one clause matches and every constrained dimension has
a value in its array. Enumerate values when you need a set such as all
modal-bearing cells. Do not use free-form code, regexes, negation operators,
item-format fields, lexical lemmas, or source IDs.

Prefer hypotheses that are linguistically coherent, reusable, independently
interpretable, measurable in more than one cell where the universe permits,
parsimonious, compositional, and pedagogically relevant. Do not add a column
merely to increase matrix rank. Do not treat response format as knowledge.
When the schema lacks distinctions needed for a good hypothesis (for example
modal function, lexical morphology, or person/number), say so rather than
fabricating them.
